The Arabian toothcarp (Aphanius dispar) is a small, hardy cyprinodontid that inhabits brackish coastal pools and hypersaline lagoons across the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa. Neonates emerge at a remarkably small size, with a wet weight at birth of approximately 0.0018 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.0018 grams], a value derived from an egg diameter of about 1.5 millimeters. This minute starting mass reflects the constrained yolk provisioning typical of small-bodied cyprinodontiforms that inhabit variable, often extreme salinity environments. The newly hatched fry must begin foraging on microscopic algae and zooplankton almost immediately, as the limited yolk reserves are quickly exhausted.

Growth in Aphanius dispar proceeds rapidly toward the onset of sexual maturity, which occurs at a total length at puberty of 3 centimeters [Lp = 3 centimeters], a threshold reached within the first couple of months of life. Individuals continue to grow after maturity, ultimately attaining a total length of 7 centimeters [Li = 7 centimeters], with a corresponding ultimate wet weight of 3.6 grams [Wwi = 3.6 grams]. This modest adult body size is characteristic of the genus, which favors small, ephemeral desert pools and coastal sabkhas where larger predatory fish are typically absent.

Reproductive output in this species is substantial for its diminutive size. Under a stable water temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C], females produce a modest number of eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = a modest number of eggs per spawning event], with spawning occurring repeatedly throughout an extended breeding season [F_R_i = spawning occurring repeatedly throughout an extended breeding season], yielding a maximum reproductive rate of approximately 200 offspring per year [Ri = approximately 200 offspring per year]. This high-frequency, iteroparous spawning strategy allows populations to rebound quickly following the boom-and-bust conditions typical of shallow, evaporation-prone habitats.

Longevity in Aphanius dispar is relatively short, with a maximum recorded lifespan of approximately 4 years [am = approximately 4 years] at the same reference temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C]. This compressed lifespan, combined with rapid early maturation and sustained annual fecundity, reflects a fast-paced life-history strategy well suited to the unpredictable, often harsh thermal and osmotic conditions of the species' native pools and lagoons. The combination of a 3-centimeter pubertal length (3 cm) [Lp = 3 cm] and a 7-centimeter ultimate length (7 cm) [Li = 7 cm] situates this species among the smallest of the toothcarps, an adaptation that likely facilitates its persistence in isolated, resource-limited desert waters.
